source_statement: Exact-BSD, Prop single:logarithm (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/05-single.tex:762-773), verbatim: 'If ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=1 and P in E(Q) is nontorsion, then log_omega z_b/(log_omega P)^2 = +/- d_0 L'(E,1)/(Omega_0 H(P)). The right-hand quotient is rational, and is interpreted in Q_p. The height is exactly the height H fixed in the introduction.' Standing hypotheses (05-single.tex:3-10): p odd; E/Q non-CM; analytic rank 0 or 1; GZK rank and finiteness in force; z_b the smoothed square class at the trivial character; d_0=Delta(0) prod_{q in S_f} P_q(1) (:748-751). Its proof (:1249-1272) uses: an auxiliary K_b=Q(sqrt(-D)), -D<-4 odd, all primes of 2Np split, L(f x eps,1)!=0, obtained from Lemma classical:auxiliary-fields 'because w(E)=-1' (:775-781); Lemma single:height-direction (:812-822: horizontal sequence r_i -> 1 in Z_p, lambda_i:(Z/r_i)^x ->> Z/p^{m_i}, bilinear tame heights with h^{K_b}=2h^Q and h^Q(P,P)!=0); Lemma single:cup (6) (:925-933); Lemma single:spectral (7) (:981-988) which imports three finite-character identities from the two-primary paper [B] section 6 (:998-1009); and the split Gross-Zagier formula classical:gross-zagier (:1255-1258). Prop single:period-law (2) (:299-312): for even nu of conductor | M the omega-coordinate of exp^*(z_nu) is +/- Delta_nu L^{(M)}(f,nu,1)/Omega_0 delta_xi(a); square order with A=1 has an integral combination with delta(a)=1; rectangular order has some A=p^k, xi with delta_xi(a)!=0 (via Rohrlich as [Kato, Thm 13.5(2)]). Prop single:center (8) (:1276-1285): X(E)=v_p(U(0))>=0 'at every odd coefficient prime, for all reduction types and all residual representations of the non-CM curve'. Pointwise 2-converse, Prop nv:local-witness (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026/build/sections/nonvanishing.tex:9-17), verbatim: 'Fix an elliptic curve A/Q and a nonempty filter of fundamental discriminants prime to 2N_A, with specified real sign and unit squareclasses at finitely many primes. If the root number in the filter is +1, it contains d of arbitrarily large absolute value with L(A^{(d)},1)!=0. If the root number is -1, it contains such d with L'(A^{(d)},1)!=0. Any additional finite set of primes may be excluded.' Prop nv:rough (:19-26): absolute A_0 with omega(d)<=A_0 in the +1 case. Proof imports Waldspurger 1981 (nonnegativity, :388-389), Heath-Brown 1995 quadratic large sieve (:101-102), Gelbart-Jacquet symmetric square (:237-238), Friedlander-Iwaniec lower linear sieve (:410), Hoffstein-Luo 1997 model (:28-30); the first-moment asymptotics S_{0,b}, S_{1,1} are Lemma nv:moment (:57-79). Two-primary, Lemma alternation-imaginary:alternation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026/build/sections/12-alternation-imaginary.tex:18-23): for V=Ind_K^Q(T chi), T a free plane with perfect alternating e, chi anticyclotomic, local conditions (i) one unrestricted coordinate at a split prime pair, the other strict (or zero), (ii) at newly allowed odd discriminant primes q, T good and unramified and chi unramified over K with unramified cochains; then for regular s, <x, partial x>=0 (H1). Cor :54-59: generic and special H^1 dimensions have the same parity. Exact-BSD Lemma theta:cut-moments (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/07-theta.tex:421-445) and Prop extraction:theta-implication (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/08-extraction.tex:28-42: if b_w^0 in a horizontal height-one prime then one of H^1_{prim,a}(K,V chi), H^1_{prim,a}(K,V' chi) is nonzero over Frac(R/p)) are as the Oct-6 audit and Codex (REPORT item (c)) describe. Grade for all of the above: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated, no Lean; history.md:25 records only a citation edit for Exact-BSD; none of the three manuscripts is withdrawn).
what_it_would_need: To become an input to any seed obligation this lead would need a theorem it does not contain. Per obligation: FIN uniform part: needs cofinite nonvanishing delta_p!=0 and the excess-content estimate m_p-w_p<=1 for cofinitely many good p, or the tame identity C2(p,l)=288(a_l-2)R at G2 auxiliaries for cofinitely many p. Section 5 gives a rank-one exact log comparison (5) at one fixed p with the twist's own scalar; it says nothing about the seed's two-point determinant, nothing cofinite in p, and nothing about valuations of A_p,B_p. The missing object is a rank-two analogue of (5): log of the second Kato derivative on wedge^2 E(Q) tensor Q_p equal to a rational multiple of L''(E,1)/(Omega Reg) with an exact constant, i.e. a rank-two Gross-Zagier/Perrin-Riou formula, which does not exist (lab's Aristotle PRECISE_OBSTRUCTION record). Named remainder 59, 487, 2243, 4547, 5843: nothing here; section 5's integrality proposition is for X(E) of a rank<=1 curve, and the local Haar identities (05-single.tex:1348-1356) are standard. For the twist E^{-7} (rank 0, additive at 7 with c_7 unrecorded) thm:main would give #Sha(E^{-7})[p^infty] at every p, but no lab chain consumes #Sha(E^{-7}) (K-route bound, plectic route and Q36 use only its corank 0 / L(E^{-7},1)!=0, both already retained); so even a verified version adds no seed input. ORDER9 / Q36: need #Sha or q_E rationality for E itself; the section's anchors are rank<=1 Gross-Zagier (classical:gross-zagier, :1255-1258) and modular-symbol rationality (:969-979). TH at 5843: the horizontal sequences in section 5 are cyclotomic/tame characters of prime conductor r_i -> 1 at good r_i (:793-811), not level-raised anticyclotomic theta elements at a multiplicative prime inert in K; nothing addresses c_1(lambda_l) or the FG25 Remark 3.5 exceptional zero. Cost reduction: none; no computation in the lab (Ota witnesses c_2(theta_l) at 59, 487; B.18 production symbols; TH; Shii theta/Fitting) is shortened by a normalization formula. If the lab nevertheless wants a rank-one normalization testbed on E^{-23}, the needed inputs are already available at published grade and should be used instead of this preprint: Kato's period formula and (c,d)-smoothing (Kato 2004 section 13, which section 5 itself cites via [Kato, Thm 9.5, 13.5(2)]) and the proved rank-one Perrin-Riou conjecture (Bertolini-Darmon-Venerucci; Buyukboduk-Pollack-Sasaki) at good ordinary p>=5 with the usual image hypotheses; the lab would have to check those hypotheses for E^{-23} at the chosen p (conductor 529N, additive at 23) and would still obtain only a p-unit/normalization check, not m_p-w_p.
obligation: None served. At most a normalization cross-check (sign, smoothing factor Delta_nu, omitted Euler factors, period Omega_0 vs Omega_E) for the lab's transported smoothed Kato derivative, on a rank-one twist; this touches no FIN/ORDER9/Q36/TH item and no named prime, and is better sourced from published Kato section 13 and the published rank-one Perrin-Riou-conjecture theorems than from this preprint.
new_observation: N1 (hypothesis Codex and the Oct-6 audit did not flag): the 'per-prime engine' of sections 7-8 is not rank-free in its setup. 07-theta.tex:4-5 opens 'Fix the odd prime p and the fields K,F,L chosen in Section classical', and those fields come from Lemma classical:auxiliary-fields (02-classical.tex:115-139), whose hypothesis is 'analytic rank r in {0,1}' with twist ranks (1-r,1-r,r) and simple zeros of L(E/K,s), L(E^{D'}/K,s); for r=2 clause (ii) is void (rank -1). 09-unit.tex:4 and 10-center.tex:12,146 also call that lemma, and 09-unit.tex:290 calls vertical:parity (04-vertical.tex:243-266), whose proof uses 'The simple-zero choices give one compact Selmer line from points'. So reusing the moment bound theta:cut-moments for the seed would first require re-proving the auxiliary-field lemma without clause (ii) and replacing the one-line acyclicity; the lemma statement being rank-free does not make the engine rank-free. N2 (published replacement, better grade): Prop nv:local-witness is, for a fixed curve, the content of published theorems on quadratic twists with prescribed local conditions (Bump-Friedberg-Hoffstein 1990, Friedberg-Hoffstein 1995; also Murty-Murty 1991 for the derivative case); the pointwise paper's references.bib does not cite them (only Hoffstein-Luo 1997, Waldspurger, Heath-Brown, Iwaniec 1990, Radziwill-Soundararajan, Friedlander-Iwaniec, Gelbart-Jacquet), whereas the two-primary paper cites FH95 and BFH90 at 12-alternation-imaginary.tex:82 for the same purpose. Only Prop nv:rough (absolute bound omega(d)<=A_0) is new, and the seed has no use for bounded-factor twists. So the 'twist witness' half of the lead should be cited, if ever, at published grade, not IMPORTED_PREPRINT. N3 (what (5) is): Prop single:logarithm is a rank-one Perrin-Riou-conjecture statement (Kato class at the trivial character = log of a rational point times the exact BSD rational constant), claimed for every odd p, all reduction types and all residual images of a non-CM curve (05-single.tex:1282-1284), which exceeds the published scope (good ordinary p with image hypotheses). Its proof is thin at exactly the new part: the p-adic biextension tame height is imported from the dyadic paper (two-primary 06-tame.tex:273-285, coefficient prime 2, 'mod 2^{m_i}') with 'verifying its p-power version here' in one paragraph (05-single.tex:864-879), and the spectral identity (7) imports three unproved-here finite-character identities from [B] section 6 (:998-1009). Rank-one testbed use would thus be testing an unreviewed proof against a published theorem, i.e. backwards. N4 (K-A location): section 5's identification 'Finite Sha identifies this line with E(Q) tensor Q_p' (05-single.tex:757) and the standing 'finiteness conclusions ... in force' (:9-10) are GZK-supplied for rank<=1; any transplant of the section's determinant-coordinate argument to E itself would have FIN as an input, a K-A kill independent of the rank-two anchor problem. Codex noted the finite-Sha use (DIRECT_BSD_AUDIT.md:138-147) but not that it is by itself a kill for E. N5 (section 12 local hypothesis vs the seed): the alternation lemma's condition (i) 'one unrestricted coordinate at a split prime pair' needs p split in K; for K=Q(sqrt(-7)) that holds at 2, 487, 4547 and fails at 3, 59, 2243, 5843 (inert), so even as structure it is not available at three of the five remainder primes without changing K. N6 (GitHub/Codex currency check requested by the user): git ls-remote on the authorized lab remote (Bome2017/bsd-seed-lab) shows research/state-sync-2026-10-04 at 4a251748, matching SEED_CONTEXT's stated head, so lab_latest/CURRENT_STATE.md and the Codex 10-11 screen are current; the local checkout is on research/plectic-step2-return at 235e081a and was not modified. The KATO_CONTENT_BOUND return directories cited by CURRENT_STATE.md are not present in the lab_latest export, so the lab's exact smoothing/normalization of delta_p could not be compared line by line here.
risks: K-A: section 5 assumes GZK finiteness and rank<=1 throughout; using any of its determinant/central-coordinate statements for E would assume FIN. K-RANK2: Prop single:logarithm, the height-direction lemma and the spectral identity are rank-one by statement; they apply to E^{-23} (rank 1 under the retained certificate) or E^{-7} (rank 0), never to E; a scalar obtained on a twist is the twist's. K-GRADE: all three manuscripts are IMPORTED_PREPRINT; the Exact-BSD proof of (5) depends on the two-primary paper [B] section 6 and on the Selmer-converse paper [C]; a chain of three unrefereed preprints must not be promoted by a numerical check on one twist. Misuse risk: a successful rank-one check of (2)/(5) on E^{-23} would be 'evidence about that test', not about the seed's normalization at any other p nor about m_p-w_p; it could be misread as validating the manuscript. Residual uncertainty in this assessment: I did not re-derive the three finite-character identities imported from [B] section 6, nor the sieve constants of nv:moment; the published-theorem attributions in N2/N3 (BFH90, FH95, Murty-Murty, BDV, BPS) are from memory and their exact hypothesis clauses (local conditions, p good ordinary, image) must be checked against the papers before the lab cites them. No code from the clone was run; no lab file was modified.
